title: How Cockroaches Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explore cockroaches: their reputation as dirty insects and how they groom themselves, the four or so common species (German, American, brown-banded, oriental) and how they spread via travel and containers, their survival of the dinosaur extinction and questions about surviving nuclear war, body anatomy (head, thorax, abdomen, compound eyes, antennae, mouthparts, legs, heart and open circulatory system, fat body, digestive system with crop and proventriculus, cerci), breathing through spiracles and decapitated survival for about a week, reproduction (oothecae, ovoviviparity, viviparity, high offspring counts), social behavior and collective decision-making, a robotic cockroach called iSpot used to lead roaches, and practical advice on keeping roaches out of homes (sealing cracks, bait traps, cleaning, natural repellents, myths about ultrasonic devices). The episode also includes a sponsor-style break reading an anecdote about a self-experimenter who got soap in his eye and water up his nose, plus closing listener information and an unrelated X-Files and fungus digression.

segments.title: Opening banter: Lacucaracha and X-Files
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the song La Cucaracha, tequila, and an X-Files cockroach episode, and mention watching reruns.

segments.title: Cockroach cleanliness and grooming
segments.summary: Cockroaches are said to be clean groomers who keep their antennae and feet clean; a swab study suggests a human's hands carried more bacteria than a roach's foot. Hosts discuss roaches as disease carriers and their feeding on waste, and Josh and Chuck debate killing roaches.

segments.title: Species, spread, and nocturnal habits
segments.summary: There are more than 4,000 cockroach species, but mainly four cause home infestations: German, American, brown-banded, and oriental, with the German and American most common in the US. Roaches spread via travel on airplanes, boats, shipping containers and moving boxes. Roaches are nocturnal, fast, and reproduce quickly.

segments.title: Extinction survival and nuclear war
segments.summary: Cockroaches have existed for about 300 million years, predating dinosaurs and surviving their extinction. Hosts discuss whether they would survive nuclear war; they are less susceptible to radiation than humans but likely would not survive nuclear winter.

segments.title: Body anatomy: head, thorax, abdomen, and head decapitation
segments.summary: Roaches are about half an inch to two inches long with downward-pointing heads and three body regions. Males have flight wings, females have vestigial wings. They molt, and bursicon hardens the exoskeleton. Roaches can regrow limbs. The brain is not central; ganglia let a roach live about a week after decapitation, dying of thirst because they breathe through spiracles.

segments.title: Eyes, antennae, mouthparts, and legs
segments.summary: Compound eyes, movable antennae that sense pheromones and odors, and mouthparts including mandibles and maxillae for chewing. Legs are named pro-, meso-, and metathoracic; the front legs brake, middle legs steer, rear legs propel. Roaches can move about 50 body lengths per second and run fast, with hooked tarsi that allow walking on ceilings.

segments.title: Circulation, digestion, and cerci
segments.summary: Roaches have an open circulatory system with a heart that moves hemolymph through hemocoels, not oxygen-carrying red blood, and a fat body that stores fat. Digestion includes a crop and a gizzard-like proventriculus that pulverizes food, and cerci that detect air currents so roaches can dodge swats.

segments.title: Reproduction, oothecae, and social behavior
segments.summary: Females release pheromones and males court with wing flapping before mating. Reproduction modes include ootheca egg cases carried or deposited, ovoviviparity, and viviparity. German cockroaches can produce large numbers of offspring. Roaches live in groups and collectively choose roosts; a robotic roach called iSpot was used to lead colonies with pheromones.

segments.title: Keeping roaches out of the home
segments.summary: Advice includes sealing cracks as small as 1.5 millimeters, using bait traps to track roaches, cleaning up food and crumbs, using poisons as a last resort or calling an exterminator, and natural repellents like boric acid-like options, catnip, and bay leaves. Ultrasonic devices are said not to work.
